Test a full-pool weighted combination using inverse_error to see if including weaker models helps robustness given trend-dominated, unstable ranking.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust trimmed mean over all models may reduce the influence of outliers.
Try a weighted softmax_neg_error combination on the full pool to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over trimmed mean.
test a robust dba combination on the smaller, stable pool4 to see if focused weighting improves over trimmed mean in this trend‑dominated series.
Testing a per‑pool weighted strategy on the smaller, more stable pool4 using softmax_neg_error to see if aggressive weighting on the top correlated models improves over trimmed mean.
test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the best_per_horizon handle (w6) on the full pool to see if horizon‑specific selection improves over global weighted.
Ranking is unstable and several models are correlated; a forward‐selection based weight may capture complementary strengths better than simple inverse error.
Try a per‑horizon weighted mean using the top‑k per‑horizon handle (w8) on the full model pool to capture horizon‑specific strengths, given the unstable ranking and trend‑dominated regime.
ranking instability and many correlated groups suggest a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture complementary strengths across horizons.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9987. Series context: trend strength 0.9591 and seasonal strength 0.2553; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.166); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.526.
